discoveries.headline: Australia's first crypto law, explained
discoveries.why: The Law Society Journal walks through the Digital Assets Framework law Parliament passed on 1 April 2026: crypto exchanges and custody providers now need an Australian Financial Services Licence, with 18 months to comply. Lawyers including Piper Alderman's Steven Pettigrove and NXT Law's Michael Bacina explain what it means for consumer protection and custody. A clear primer on the rules that now sit behind the platforms Australians use. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: COP31's draft drops fossil fuels
discoveries.why: As the Antalya climate talks run past their Friday deadline, Reuters reports that the revised draft deal stripped out both earlier references to fossil fuels. It acknowledges warming could exceed 1.5 degrees and calls for 'deep, rapid and sustained' emissions cuts, and Australia, leading the negotiations, expects the text to change again. A quick read to understand the headlines this weekend.
discoveries.meta_credit: Reuters · William James and Valerie Volcovici

discoveries.headline: Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026
discoveries.why: Federico Veronesi's 'The Aftermath', taken in Namibia's Huab River Valley, won the top prize from 65,000 entries across 121 countries and territories. Don't miss Oscar Whitfield's 'Labour of Love', the Young Wildlife Photographer winner, or Tony Wu's 'Making Morays' under water. A weekend scroll that will remind you how wild and wonderful the world still is.
discoveries.meta_credit: Discover Wildlife · Sophie Ellis · Natural History Museum, London

discoveries.headline: Medicine for the lonely heart
discoveries.why: In her latest talk, Tara Brach looks at how fear of rejection and feelings of unworthiness keep us guarded, even with people we love. With stories, guided reflection and her RAIN practice, she invites you to meet loneliness with tenderness instead of blame. Free to stream, and a gentle companion for a Saturday walk.

discoveries.headline: What we can't measure about AI yet
discoveries.why: Manchester business scholar Carlo Cordasco starts with a surprise: respected doctors opposed anaesthesia on sound evidence, because they couldn't foresee the surgery it would make possible. He argues AI's costs are easy to see while its biggest benefits may depend on practices that don't exist yet, and proposes 'recoverability' as a test for how cautious to be. A thoughtful long read, or a 25-minute listen.
discoveries.meta_credit: Aeon · Carlo Cordasco · edited by Nigel Warburton

discoveries.headline: Miss Kaninna takes home an ARIA
discoveries.why: At the 40th ARIA Awards, Yorta Yorta, Dja Dja Wurrung, Kalkadoon and Yirendali artist Miss Kaninna won Best Hip Hop/Rap Release for BLACKPRINT, the debut mixtape she released independently. The full winners list is a great map of Australian music right now, from Tame Impala's seven wins to Emma Donovan and Donny Benét. Start with BLACKPRINT this weekend.

discoveries.headline: Four weeks of food, a younger biological age
discoveries.why: University of Sydney researchers put 104 people aged 65 to 75 on one of four diets for four weeks and tracked biological age using 20 blood markers, including cholesterol and insulin. Three of the four diets lowered it, with the clearest result from a high-carbohydrate omnivorous diet. The authors call it preliminary, but it's a hopeful sign that what's on your plate matters at any age. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: University of Sydney · Dr Caitlin Andrews and A/Prof Alistair Senior, Charles Perkins Centre

discoveries.headline: A free yoga practice for every day
discoveries.why: Adriene Mishler's free November calendar gives you a practice for every day of the month, each linked to a YouTube playlist. No sign-up, no guesswork about what to do today: just open it and press play. A lovely way to make yoga one of your weekend rituals.

discoveries.headline: How to get stronger
discoveries.why: Harvard Medical School's Edward Phillips keeps it simple: pick a weight you can lift eight to 12 times, go heavier when 12 feels easy, and use body-weight moves like squats, push-ups and heel raises if you're starting out. He also explains why fewer than one in three US adults meet the strength guideline, and how to handle next-day soreness. A four-minute read to build stronger rituals.
discoveries.meta_credit: Harvard Gazette · Sy Boles · Edward Phillips, Harvard Medical School
